ER-negative status and a family history (of hereditary breast and/or ovarian) cancer are predictive of having BRCA1 and/ or BRCA2 mutations in an Asian population.

the development of a predictive model that may help to identify patients who are likely to have deleterious mutations in BRCA genes, in the Asian population.

ER-negative, TNBC and younger patients with a FH of HBOC should be tested for BRCA mutations, in an Asian context.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of ER negativity, TNBC status, and a FH of HBOC are strong factors predicting a BRCA mutation.
BRCA testing should be offered to all TNBC patients, regardless of their FH, and to all patients with a strong FH, regardless of TNBC status.
BRCA testing should be offered in all patients who have TNBC, ER-negative breast cancer, and those with a strong family history of breast and ovarian cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ER-negative status and TNBC status are strong predictive factors for BRCAs, and that younger age and strong FH of HBOCs are also strong predictive factors.
